content.text:
The drawing shows a quaternary nitrogen with a + charge bearing three methyl groups (CH3, H3C and H3C). The fourth substituent on nitrogen is a CH2, which connects to a carboxylate carbon. That carbon has a double bond to O and a single bond to O⁻. This is glycine betaine.

SMILES: C[N+](C)(C)CC(=O)[O-]
